questions: Are consecutive delimiters (e.g., multiple commas or spaces) treated as a single delimiter, or do they produce empty strings in the result?
What qualifies as a 'standard delimiter'? Is it only commas and spaces, or also tabs, newlines, punctuation, etc.?
Should leading or trailing delimiters be ignored (trimmed), or do they create empty strings at the start/end of the array?
Is the delimiter set fixed (comma and space) or locale-dependent (like whitespace in Python's split())?
Should words retain their original casing, or be normalized (e.g., lowercased)?
If the input contains only delimiters (e.g., ', ,, '), should the output be an empty array or an array with empty strings?
Are delimiters inside quoted substrings (if any) considered part of the word or as delimiters?
Should the function handle Unicode spaces or commas (e.g., non-breaking spaces) as delimiters?
